get.description:
Paywall configuration — tier names, prices, per-feature caps and labels.
Public so the guest paywall renders without auth. Single source of truth
is `billing.LIMITS` + the marketing constants in `billing.py`.

Public health + surface the support email so the iOS Privacy Policy /
feedback flows never hardcode it. Falls back to SMTP_USER (then GMAIL_USER)
if SUPPORT_EMAIL isn't set so the app always has a valid contact.

v2.0: also surfaces the kill-switch fields the iOS bootstrap reads to
decide whether to show the "Update required" gate. `min_supported_version`
is the human-readable marketing version string; `min_supported_build` is
the monotonic CFBundleVersion the client compares against. When
`force_update_required` is True, the client blocks all UI behind the
update gate regardless of which build is running.

v2.0 feature-flag endpoint. iOS `RemoteConfigStore` polls this on
launch and every 30 min to decide which surfaces are live. Public
(no auth) so the widget extension can read it without a bearer token.

Each flag's default lives in the iOS binary (`FeatureFlag.defaultValue`
in `FeatureFlags.swift`); this endpoint only OVERRIDES defaults — an
absent key means "use the binary's default."

`killed_surfaces` is the immediate kill-switch: any flag named here is
forced false on the client regardless of `flags[key]`. Used to roll a
surface back without an App Store submission.

Env-driven for now (no admin UI yet). Format:
    FORTE_FLAGS_JSON='{"use_new_ia": true, "use_observable_session": true}'
    FORTE_KILLED_SURFACES='use_live_activity,use_interactive_widget'
    MIN_SUPPORTED_BUILD='2026050101'
    FORCE_UPDATE_REQUIRED='false'

Permanently delete the user and every row that references them.

that supports account creation.

post.description:
Kick off a v2 search (wider sourcing + scam filter + posts) and
return its task_id.

**Idempotent under repeated calls.** Two collapse windows protect
the user from being billed for duplicate work:

  • In-flight: a hit while an earlier task is still running returns
    that task's id. Quota check is skipped — the work is already
    happening and already paid for.
  • Cooldown: a hit within ~90s of a successful scan, against the
    SAME profile revision, replays the previous task_id. Same
    billing-free behaviour.

A real new background scan only spawns when neither collapse
applies; only that path runs `billing.require` + `billing.record`.
Errored tasks are never replayed — a retry on a failed scan goes
through as a fresh spawn.

Response: `{"task_id", "fresh": bool, "reason": str}`. iOS clients
that ignore the two new fields keep working unchanged.

iOS poll loop: GET /seeker/v2/search/{task_id} until status='done'.
